contradictions.rationale: Same educator, two sources, on the figure both present as the realistic monthly return. Source #6: '8 to 10% a month ... that is a fact anybody can do that', with 50% per month explicitly unrealistic. Source #8: 'I wanna make seven twelve fifteen percent a month', then 'if you can make seven ten percent on any account'. The ranges overlap but do not match, and 15% sits outside the earlier stated ceiling. Filed MINOR: both are unevidenced performance figures that are already blocked from promotion, so the disagreement changes nothing operationally. Recorded because the library's practice is to log numeric drift rather than average it away.

normalization.reversibilityProof: Reassembly of the recorded parts equals the source line; asserted for every transformed line at generation time.

openQuestions.reason: This source's central lesson is that a target should not be cut because the dollar figure feels large. It does not say whether a target may be cut for a MARKET reason - opposing structure, a session ending, a counter-signal. Source #5's 'set and forget' framing implies never; this source only rules out the emotional case. The distinction matters for any trade-management rule and is not made.
openQuestions.text: Is the take-profit ever moved for a market reason, and if so on what signal?

openQuestions.reason: A $650-700 fee is presented as convertible into a 100K account and thence into $5,000 from a single 1:2 trade. **The failure branch is absent**: no pass rate, no mention that the fee is lost on breach, no reference to the daily-loss and drawdown rules that source #6 said constrain risk banding. A specific provider is named. Recorded as a materially incomplete presentation of a paid product, not as trading knowledge.
openQuestions.text: What is the evaluation pass rate, and what happens to the fee when a trader fails?

openQuestions.reason: Three overlapping ranges across two sources, none evidenced and none accompanied by a drawdown figure. See the contradiction filed in this ingestion. MOGO must not average or pick.
openQuestions.text: Which monthly return figure is the claim - 7-10%, 8-10%, or 7/12/15%?

openQuestions.reason: Unsourced, like '99% of traders lose money' and 'retail is 3% of the market'. The argument it supports - that individual size is insignificant - is also in tension with source #3's position that retail being 3% of the market means retail stops are not worth hunting. Both use market-scale figures to argue different things.
openQuestions.text: What is the source for the 6.3 trillion daily turnover figure, and does it support the argument?

openQuestions.reason: He names the rule, tells viewers to write it down, then states he personally folds the 10% into investment. Openly stated as his own choice rather than concealed, so it is an exception rather than a contradiction - but it is the second instance in two sources of practice diverging from a stated rule, after the proximity tolerance in source #7.

Presented as covering '100% of your income' and 'my whole entire life as a whole'. Whether trading profits enter the same allocation, and whether the 30% investment tranche can include funding the trading account itself, is not stated. **This is a personal-finance rule, not a trading rule**, and is typed 'other' so it cannot be mistaken for one.
openQuestions.text: Does the 30/30/30/10 rule apply to trading profits, to all income, or to both?

openQuestions.reason: He prescribes not showing open positions to others while operating a community in which he shows his own setups and reviews members' trades weekly. Plausibly distinguishable - showing a setup is not the same as seeking validation on an open position - but the distinction is not drawn.
openQuestions.text: How does 'don't show anybody' sit alongside running a paid community and live calls?

openQuestions.reason: EIGHT Alex G sources, `stop_rule` still 0. This source discusses 1:4 and 1:2 risk-to-reward, a $650 risk figure and a 100K account, and never states where the stop that defines that risk is placed. See BACKLOG-002/A1-STOP.

The published title says 'PT 2'; the spoken content says 'video number one official of the psychology series' and 'episode three' of the podcast. Second title/content discrepancy from this channel after the $1000/day vs $500/day mismatch in source #5. Both recorded; neither resolved.
openQuestions.text: Is this psychology video part 1 or part 2?
